scope: Independent substantive SCI and ZHEN review of authored n116/n117 bilingual text only.

sourceConsumed.use: Upstream consumed-once evidence for six source pages and eleven raw PNGs. No source page, crop, or image was reopened or independently reapproved here.

loop.use: Uniform external field, closed-loop force cancellation, planar enclosed area, current-selected normal, turn-count dependence, and torque orientation.
loop.notImported: No examples, new equations, numerical data, or figures.

matter.use: Microscopic magnetic moments and their alignment, with equivalent-current pictures treated as models.
matter.excludedOpening: The literal classical electron-orbit and spinning-sphere account is not reproduced in either n116 template.
matter.notImported: No magnetic-domain figures, tables, new equations, or numerical data.

primaryContext.siCheckBasis: The retained source unit equation and independent dimensional reasoning, not the unused general-SI redirect.

method.comparison: Read every retained source prose block and every current localized template in full; independently evaluate the physical claims and source coverage, then compare the Chinese and English conditions, meanings, notation, units, and textual figure references.
method.mechanicalChecks: Read-only Node assertions verified all twelve per-record source/template/draft hash bindings, exact embedded source snapshots, exact source_text for every block, unchanged source block order/identity/references, and draft/template prose equivalence after removing whitespace.
method.proseFlowChecks: Ran the repository prose_flow.mjs --json against each of the four current templates. These outputs establish actual textual paragraph anchors only, not scientific, image, or display approval.
method.technicalDiagnostic: An initial draft/template comparison collapsed whitespace to spaces and failed on the known insertion of a newline after Chinese punctuation. A corrected whitespace-insensitive comparison passed without changing any input. This was a comparison-method error, not a content verdict.
method.approvalBasis: The independent substantive judgments below, not author declarations, upstream source approval, hashes alone, or native output alone.

findings.sourceClaim: The Earth weak-field demonstration explicitly permits a comparatively large coil: 然而，线圈的大小可以是比较大的.
findings.observed: Both current templates retain more turns or larger current and freedom about two axes, but neither retains the source's permitted larger physical coil size.
findings.reason: This is an apparatus-condition omission, not a request to restore obsolete cultural wording. It removes the distinction between the preceding small local probe and a larger coil usable in the Earth-field demonstration. The source snapshot still contains the claim, but the learner-facing text does not.
findings.SCI: HOLD for semantic completeness; the retained physical statements themselves are correct.
findings.ZHEN: HOLD for completeness relative to the source. The two modern languages agree with each other, but share the omission.
findings.requiredCorrection: Retain the source's larger-coil possibility in both languages specifically for this demonstration, while preserving the approximately uniform external-field condition and the small-probe distinction. No new size value, question, research, or image is needed.
findings.affectedOnlyRecheck: Recheck n116 prose[5], the corresponding bilingual draft passages, and any section_breaks anchors changed by that correction. Unchanged n116 blocks and n117 do not require a repeated full review.

phy9-c2-s5-n116.reason: Both languages retain loop/needle orientation as the motivation for a vector with magnitude and direction.
Both retain the right-hand screw rule, the current-selected normal, and Figure 243. Stable equilibrium in an approximately uniform external field is explicitly distinguished from a transient normal.
Both retain a freely turning small probe and direction determined after stable settling; damping and orientation rather than attraction are careful clarifications.
Weak Earth field, more turns/larger current, two-axis freedom, Figure 245, and regional downward inclination are retained; the source's permitted comparatively large coil is missing. D045-TEXT-01.
Permanent needle identity, S-to-N direction, stable loop-normal agreement, and Figure 244 are correct and bilingual-equivalent.
Figures 246/247, local Earth-field probing, and horizontal-axis access to dip are retained. A horizontally constrained needle is not claimed to reveal the full three-dimensional direction.

Both retain circular tangent directions in planes perpendicular to the straight wire and the screw rule with advance along conventional current. Neither replaces the tangent by a radial direction or substitutes electron motion unchanged.
Needle/loop probing of the solenoid field and Figure 249 are retained, without new quantitative claims.

Both preserve the loop/needle explanatory analogy and next-chapter reference. Microscopic moments and alignment are used carefully; no literal tiny wire coils, classical electron paths, or physically spinning electron spheres are asserted.

phy9-c2-s5-n117.reason: Both retain the preceding vector-direction discussion and the question of determining the field quantity's magnitude.
Force/test-charge ratio and independence from probe charge are retained with a non-disturbing-probe condition; both distinguish the field from the measuring object.

Zero net magnetic force and no magnetic-force acceleration of the center of mass are explicitly conditional on an external field uniform over the whole closed loop. Nonzero individual segment forces are not denied. No such zero-force assertion is extended to a nonuniform field.
Net force is distinguished from torque. Orientation, enclosed area, current, and shape independence are correctly scoped to a planar loop in a fixed uniform external field.

Single-turn current I, loop plane perpendicular to the pole-to-pole field direction, zero torque, current-dependent stretching, and untwisted suspension at the source's Figure 250 orientation are retained. The stretching statement is not generalized to arbitrary reversed current.
Both preserve the restoring torque toward the stated stable Figure 250 orientation and allow oscillation/settling. They do not identify the maximum-torque orientation as stable.
Figure 251 suspension twisting supplies an opposing balancing torque, not a changed field definition.

Figure 252 has the field in the loop plane and the normal perpendicular to it, so torque magnitude is maximal. The largest balancing twist is explicitly limited to the discussed elastic measurement range.

Maximum torque proportional to IS is retained for the same uniform external field and single-turn planar loop; S is enclosed area. English max is a descriptive-subscript translation, not a new variable or equation.

B equals maximum torque divided by IS, not arbitrary instantaneous torque. Equation (11-1), non-disturbing small probe, approximate uniformity, and the separate need to account for multiple turns are bilingual-equivalent.
Magnitude and direction at every point describe the field; one local measurement is not substituted for the whole spatial field.
E/B vector analogy is retained while their definitions and probe responses are distinguished.

The source's 1 ampere, 1 square meter, and 1 newton-meter maximum torque are preserved. The unit ratio reduces from N*m/(A*m^2) to N/(A*m); enclosed area is distinguished from wire cross-section. English N/A/m and max localize unit names and the descriptive label only.

Both retain the unit's namesake as the real scientist Tesla, not a fictional replacement or product. ZH declares term 特斯拉; EN declares term Tesla with source_term 特斯拉 and translation. Removal of the historical geopolitical descriptor/printed initial is treated as intentional context clarification, not loss of the named person's identity.
